_summary: Read in full on 2026-09-24. A subset run between changes (CLAUDE.md, 'Promoting a candidate'): the eight cases the changes since run 16 touch, on the candidate at cd7c8d8 (the examples without read dates, the reworded R and recovery examples, the number-provenance lint, the formula lint), the first run on the troid-eval key. Not a promotion run: it counts toward no rule. 7 of 8 passed automatically; under the checks added from this read, 5. No critical error. The errors: ex-r (the source) says the daily limit is a fixed amount of the initial balance 'per Bitfunded's help centre and Terms of Use', where its source is the Bitfunded FAQ (the sources list has it right); b-stop (the math) writes its formula in words, 'the risk divided by the distance between entry and stop, plus a fee amount per unit', which reads as risk ÷ distance + fee (its example has it right, 500 ÷ (1,292 + 62.30)); p-size (the math) says troid's four defaults 'none change the sizing above but affect margin and liquidation distance' (the 35% cap and the 2R target affect neither), in a list of troid's assumptions the service gives again under the answer; o-montecarlo (the method) is a lint rewrite that stood in for its draft: it opens 'That result models …', pointing at a result the reader never saw, never says ask troid runs no simulation, drops the 0.21R and 45.45% trade_math computed, and sits under a tier line calling troid's simulated years DERIVED. Fixed since run 16: ex-r gives no undated 4% and every number comes from a tool; b-stop computes no ratio in prose; b-leverage has its formula; o-montecarlo writes no p·W. Staged from this read, the candidate's: a rewrite stands only when it trips fewer notes than its draft and fixes at least one; a formula line carries an equals sign; a reply never opens on a result the reader never saw; the tier line says MODELLED when a reply quotes troid's Monte Carlo; troid's assumptions are listed once, by the service. Checks added to match. Tokens: $0.5161 for the eight cases at the recorded prices, $0.0645 a case on average; ex-r, the first case, paid most of the cache writes ($0.2111).
